proof_attempt_summary: Three proposal angles attempted compact critical-process inference, raw-quadratic self-normalization, and primitive learned-GPS calibration. No exact-class field theorem survived: the phase frontier required forbidden outer envelopes, while compact process/calibration remained technical and unproved; the fitted-rate obstruction is conditional on an unproved uniform same-loss bound. D0 and F were never launched, so there is no Lean output or proved headline.
tldr: Raw squared excesses can calibrate a continuous-dose empirical causal expected-shortfall ratio even when their population expectation is infinite. The proposed result characterizes the maximal shrinking two-sided neighborhood of the variance boundary on which this Gaussian calibration is uniformly valid, and supplies a legal fixed-supercritical failure witness beyond that neighborhood. The submitted compact critical window is retained exactly, with its marked crossover covariance, learned stabilized weights, continuum empirical cutoffs, and simultaneous ninety-percent band. The open quantitative frontier asks for matching process-approximation error bounds as the neighborhood expands. The claim concerns the validity of this direct empirical procedure, not efficiency relative to fitted extreme-value estimators.
gap: Scalar fixed-law Studentization, abstract triangular-array self-normalization, fixed-index empirical ES phases, and extremal regression self-normalization are established. Their inspected specifications do not identify the maximal Gaussian envelope for a causal localized empirical excess process with unknown GPS and same-record squared scores.
fill: Theorem \(\text{thm:raw-quadratic-frontier}\) gives an if-and-only-if envelope claim with constructive feasible coverage and an explicit failure witness. The open quantitative node asks for the matching approximation-error order rather than another estimator-transfer result.
